gender_fit: Neutral. Terminal green is a default; re-skin the palette to the person.
when_it_makes_sense: - Jamie, 40, lives in Slack and spreadsheets\n- A sister's 30th: 'Loading SISTER.EXE... sarcasm.dll OK'\n- A coworker's card: 'stand-up-meeting.dll... skipped'
example_in_action:
JAMIE.EXE v40.0
Loading espresso.dll ... OK
Loading snacks.dll ... OK
WARNING: punctuality.sys not found
Ready. Press any key.
what_we_need_from_the_giver: Name, age, and 1 or 2 habits or obsessions they are known for.
watch_outs: Needs reading, so keep lines short. 'Any key' must also work as a tap on phones. With reduced-motion on, show all lines at once. Offer a Skip link.

when_it_makes_sense: - The card is sent 3 days late: 'Fashionably late, by 3 days'\n- Sent a month early for a child: '27 sleeps to go'\n- Any card: the same link works before, on and after the day
example_in_action: Before: 6 days until Riley turns 9.\nToday: It's today. Riley is 9.\nAfter: Belated by 4 days. Only 361 to go until the next one.
what_we_need_from_the_giver: Birthday date (day and month, not birth year), plus a lateness or time habit if there is one.
watch_outs: Needs the day and month. Use the viewer's own date. Let the giver decide whether lateness is a joke; skip the joke if the card is late for a sensitive reason.

gender_fit: Neutral. Style follows the recipient's tastes, not gender.
when_it_makes_sense: - Any card: the opening image and link preview\n- Riley, 9, loves space: star-map letters with a tiny rabbit\n- Jamie, 40, cyclist and espresso lover: letters cut from a bike map and a coffee bag
example_in_action: J-A-M-I-E as cut-out letters on kraft paper. One letter has a coffee ring, a tiny bell hangs off the I. Subtitle: 'Forty, and only slightly late.'
what_we_need_from_the_giver: Name and at least 1 obsession or habit to steer the style.
watch_outs: Keep the name legible (contrast, size). Check unusual spellings and accents. Add alt text so screen readers read the name.

when_it_makes_sense: - A big milestone: 30, 40, 50, 'Sweet 16'\n- A child scratching to find the surprise plan\n- A card hiding a gift or plan: 'Dinner Friday, my treat'
example_in_action: Teaser: 'Scratch for your real age.'\nUnder the silver: 'Forty. Still under warranty.'
what_we_need_from_the_giver: Something worth revealing (age, plan or gift) and 1 real detail.
watch_outs: Scratching is fiddly for older thumbs and impossible for some screen-reader users: always include the tap-to-reveal button.

gender_fit: Neutral. Genre choice follows the person, not gender.
when_it_makes_sense: - A dramatic friend group\n- Jamie, 40: 'In a world where everyone leaves on time...'\n- Kids 10 to 12: 'Coming Saturday: RILEY: THE BIRTHDAY'
example_in_action:
In a world where everyone leaves on time...
one person leaves ten minutes late,
with snacks.
JAMIE: THE ARRIVAL. Rated B for Birthday.
what_we_need_from_the_giver: Name and 3 or more facts (habits, obsessions, a memory).
watch_outs: Fast cuts: no more than 3 flashes per second, and a static fallback for reduced-motion. No real film quotes, logos or studio names.

when_it_makes_sense: - The burnt dinner, the wrong train, the great printer jam\n- A sibling's 21st: 'The Trampoline Event'\n- A team card: 'The Great Stapler Incident of March'
example_in_action:
INC-0040. Severity: Mildly Legendary.
Subject arrived ten minutes 'out' to a birthday dinner for the third time, carrying snacks.
Root cause: Optimism.
Corrective action: None. Do not change.
Replays: 0. Lessons learned: 0.
what_we_need_from_the_giver: ONE real story (what happened, who was there, how it ended) that the giver is happy to share with everyone who sees the card.
watch_outs: Only use a story the giver actually told. Ask 'Is this OK for everyone who sees the card?' (group cards). Never use injuries, health scares or money trouble.

gender_fit: Neutral. Sprites are recoloured to look like the person, not gendered by default.
when_it_makes_sense: - A story with a clear beat: the chase, the wrong turn, the dog stealing dinner\n- Kids 6 to 12: them and their pet on an adventure\n- Gamers: their favourite genre as the skin (platformer, racing)
example_in_action: Scene 1 (trail): Pixel Jamie pedals. 'Ten minutes out.'\nScene 5 (cafe): the espresso machine glows.\nScene 6: friends wait on a bench. 'Worth the wait.'
what_we_need_from_the_giver: One story or habit with a clear beat, plus who else was there (a person or pet).
watch_outs: Needs a sprite engine. Sprites are not likenesses: colour palettes only. Do not depict real accidents or injuries. Keep it under 45 seconds and captions readable.

gender_fit: Neutral. Give every recipient a stylized avatar picked from a kit, not a default male figure.
when_it_makes_sense: - A single-scene story (the phone call, the wrong bus, the burnt toast)\n- A child who loves drawing and comics\n- Any adult with a signature moment: 'the night the cat...'
example_in_action:
1. Riley points at the moon: 'Bean, we're going!'
2. Bean wears a foil helmet.
3. 'Houston, we have carrots.'
4. Bean asleep in Riley's lap: 'Best crew ever.'
what_we_need_from_the_giver: One funny single-scene story or habit, plus any pet or person in it.
watch_outs: Consistent art is hard with free-form image generation: use a fixed character kit. Never generate realistic likenesses of real people, especially children. Alt text per panel.

when_it_makes_sense: - Someone with a strong routine: the 6 am runner, the Sunday gardener\n- Dad's 60th: 'The Common Dad, observed near the barbecue'\n- A friend group: 'The herd gathers at the cafe'
example_in_action: 'Here, in the wild, we find the Jamie. It has not eaten. It forages: a bag of snacks. Note the signature call: "It's fine, I'll meet you there."'
what_we_need_from_the_giver: 3 or more habits or obsessions, one memory, and the people around them.
watch_outs: Keep the narrator kind: no demeaning animal comparisons, no body or mating jokes. Narration by browser voice is optional and can sound flat; captions must stand alone.

when_it_makes_sense: - The giver has plenty of photos: trips, milestones\n- A grandparent's birthday with family snaps and grandchildren's notes\n- A long friendship: 'Year 1' to 'Year 15'
example_in_action: Front: 'Lake trip, 2019.'\nBack: 'You said ten minutes and we still had time for a swim.'
what_we_need_from_the_giver: 6 or more photos if possible, with a real memory or place per photo.
watch_outs: Confirm the giver has the right to use each photo and that group shots are fine with the others. Compress images to keep the downloadable file small. Alt text for every photo.

gender_fit: Neutral. Choose flattering, non-realistic styles for everyone.
when_it_makes_sense: - Any recipient with a good photo\n- Kids: their photo becomes a pixel hero\n- Milestone cards: the portrait doubles as the share preview
example_in_action: Photo of Jamie turns, in three steps ('Sketching...', 'Colouring...', 'Done.'), into a 16-colour pixel portrait wearing a tiny cycling cap.
what_we_need_from_the_giver: One clear, well-lit photo of the recipient, and 1 real prop or obsession to add beside the portrait.
watch_outs: Never comment on appearance. Some teens are photo-shy: make it optional. Say clearly that the photo is processed on the device. Get consent if others appear in the photo.

when_it_makes_sense: - Milestone birthdays: 40, 50, 60, 70\n- Long friendships and family cards\n- A child's 'story so far' in a parent's or grandparent's card
example_in_action:
1996: 'Learned to ride a bike. Never stopped.'
2012: 'Moved to Ottawa with two suitcases and a kettle.'
2019: 'The espresso era begins.'
Now: 'Forty, and only just getting started.'
what_we_need_from_the_giver: 4 or more real life events with a year or age (moves, first jobs, meeting the giver, big trips).
watch_outs: Never guess dates or events. Leave out painful milestones (loss, divorce, illness) unless the giver includes them and confirms. Ask before publishing ages of others in the story.

when_it_makes_sense: - Workplace friends and colleagues\n- A parent as 'manager of the household'\n- A pet's annual review, paired with the Talking Pet Cameo
example_in_action: Punctuality: 2 of 5. Consistent, in its way.\nSnack Logistics: 5 of 5. Industry-leading.\nVerdict: Promoted to friend for life.
what_we_need_from_the_giver: 4 to 6 traits or habits, and whether the review is for the person or a pet.
watch_outs: Low ratings must never touch appearance, health, money or intelligence. Keep the lowest score on a harmless quirk.

when_it_makes_sense: - A dog, cat or rabbit with a name\n- A child with a stuffed toy or an imaginary friend\n- An adult with a plant, a car or the espresso machine as the talking object
example_in_action: Tap Bean: 'Riley says I'm a space rabbit. I say she's late for carrots.'\nTap 9: 'Happy birthday. I chewed the card. Sorry. Love, Bean.'
what_we_need_from_the_giver: The pet's name and species (or a beloved object), 3 or more real details about it, and what it means to the recipient.
watch_outs: Ask whether the pet is still alive. If not, offer a gentle tribute variant or skip. Only use a pet the giver named.

when_it_makes_sense: - Tech, car and bike fans\n- Someone whose espresso habit is 'measurable'\n- Any obsession with a natural number: laps, pages, cups
example_in_action: Caffeine: 340% of control group. LEGEND.\nPunctuality: 62%. WARN.\nVerdict: Functioning perfectly. Do not fix.
what_we_need_from_the_giver: 4 to 6 real traits, quirks or obsessions that can be 'measured', and optionally a beloved object.
watch_outs: Avoid medical-sounding readings (blood pressure, weight, heart rate). Mark all numbers as illustrative. Sad-trombone sound only for harmless quirks.

gender_fit: Neutral. The default sporty look can skew 'gamer': re-skin to their interests.
when_it_makes_sense: - Sporty, gaming or collecting friends\n- Kids: a Legendary 9-year-old with 'Rabbit Whisperer' ability\n- A group gift: one card per guest
example_in_action:
JAMIE 'The Latecomer'. Legendary Friend (Cyclist).
Patience 3/10. Snack Power 10/10.
Ability, Second Wind: arrives late, and the party gets better.
"It's fine, I'll meet you there."
what_we_need_from_the_giver: Name, 4 or more traits or habits, a catchphrase if any, and optionally a photo for the art.
watch_outs: Stats must flatter. No low scores on looks or intelligence. Tilt effect needs motion permission on some phones: fall back to drag.

when_it_makes_sense: - A colleague or friend with an office sense of humour\n- Someone with a repeated pattern: always late, always 'one last thing'\n- Friends who love a satirical chart
example_in_action: 'The 4 Ps of Arriving Fashionably': Planning (optimistic), Pedalling (fast), Pit stop (coffee), Presents (snacks). Chart: arrival time vs enthusiasm.
what_we_need_from_the_giver: 3 or more habits or memories, and an audience that enjoys office humour.
watch_outs: Office jargon excludes people who never worked in an office. Keep captions plain-language and give every chart alt text. Never present data as real.

when_it_makes_sense: - Any adult or teen who enjoys 'making it official'\n- Kids: 'By royal decree...' with a big stamp\n- Parents: 'Executive Order: Dad's Day'
example_in_action: WHEREAS Jamie brings snacks; WHEREAS snacks improve every trip; NOW THEREFORE Section 1: All parties shall wait ten minutes.\n[Sign into law] then memo: 'We would wait longer.'
what_we_need_from_the_giver: 3 to 4 real facts (habits, quirks, what they are known for) and who signs.
watch_outs: No real legal claims or real government seals. Keep it obviously parody with 'Not an actual law'. Stamp sound optional.

when_it_makes_sense: - A friend with 'crimes': always late, hogs the playlist\n- Sibling roasts\n- A kid's 'Court of Cuteness'
example_in_action:
Charge 1: Arriving ten minutes out (3 counts).
Exhibit A: a bag of snacks.
Verdict: Guilty of making every trip better.
Sentence: a lifetime supply of thanks.
what_we_need_from_the_giver: 3 harmless 'crimes' (habits), 3 exhibits (memories or objects), and a witness.
watch_outs: Charges must be harmless: no theft, violence or anything that could be true. Label it as pretend. Gavel sound optional.

when_it_makes_sense: - A friend with a legendary 'signature crime'\n- Kids: 'WANTED for cuddles'\n- Outdoorsy people: a western theme
example_in_action:
WANTED: Jamie 'Ten-Minutes-Out'.
Crimes: espresso theft, snack smuggling, chronic lateness.
Last seen: on a bike, with a bag.
Reward: one coffee. Return to: the gang.
what_we_need_from_the_giver: Nickname or epithet, 4 habits, a favourite place, and a reward the giver can deliver.
watch_outs: Avoid gun imagery for children. It must never look like a real notice. Photo is optional; a silhouette works.

when_it_makes_sense: - Friends who joke about 'the small print'\n- A long-time friend group: 'Terms of Being Jamie's Friend'\n- A team card: 'Team agreement, version 40'
example_in_action: 3.2 Punctuality. Estimates of arrival are offered without warranty.\n7.1 We agree to wait anyway.\n[I agree]  [Decline] (the Decline button slides away)
what_we_need_from_the_giver: 4 to 6 real habits or quirks, plus one thing the giver truly promises.
watch_outs: Long legal text is dull on a phone: cap at 40 seconds. Keep the Accept button reachable and never trap the user.

when_it_makes_sense: - Spouse, partner or parent cards: 'User Guide: Dad v60'\n- A high-maintenance-but-lovable friend\n- A sibling who runs on snacks and sarcasm
example_in_action:
Won't start: coffee.
Runs slow after 2 pm: snack.
Sudden silence: it is thinking. Do not interrupt.
Warranty: lifetime, non-transferable.
what_we_need_from_the_giver: 3 or more real preferences, 4 habits ('symptoms'), and one sincere line for the warranty.
watch_outs: Keep troubleshooting to harmless quirks: no body, health, money or relationship 'faults'.

when_it_makes_sense: - Working adults and colleagues\n- A friend group: 'Skills: Being Late (99+)'\n- A retiree: 'Experience: 40 years of gardening'
example_in_action: Headline: Professional Snack Strategist | Espresso Evangelist.\nSkill: Being Late (99+), endorsed by Brian and Tim.\nRecommendation (dramatization): 'Would wait again.' Brian
what_we_need_from_the_giver: 4 skills or habits, real names of endorsers, and places or hobbies for 'experience'.
watch_outs: Recommendations put words in real people's mouths: label them 'dramatization' and let the giver approve. Do not imply real employment. Never use a real network's name or logo.

when_it_makes_sense: - Friend groups with a real chat culture\n- Siblings: 'The Family Group Chat'\n- Teens: the squad chat
example_in_action:
Brian: he's on his way
Tim: define 'on his way'
Jamie: ten minutes out
Brian: he said that at 6
Jamie: it's fine, I'll meet you there
what_we_need_from_the_giver: Real names of 2 to 4 friends, a running joke, and the recipient's catchphrase.
watch_outs: Simulated lines put words in real people's mouths: keep them kind, label 'Dramatization', and let the giver approve. Never include private details or real chat logs.

when_it_makes_sense: - Travel lovers and people who are always running late\n- Long-distance friends: 'Arrivals: love from afar'\n- Milestones: 'Departures: age 39 to 40'
example_in_action: 20:00  CAKE  Gate 4U  BOARDING\n19:50  JAMIE  Gate ??  DELAYED\n19:45  SNACKS  Gate 1  ON TIME
what_we_need_from_the_giver: One time or travel habit, and 5 or more real places, foods or people to use as destinations.
watch_outs: Flip animation is motion-heavy: offer a static fallback for reduced-motion. Status must not rely on colour alone.

gender_fit: Neutral. Default arcade look can read 'gamer': skin it to their world.
when_it_makes_sense: - Kids: catch falling stars and treats\n- Foodies: catch dropped dumplings\n- Jamie, 40: the cyclist catches snacks and dodges alarm clocks
example_in_action: Title: Snack Drop. Catch: croissants, oranges, energy bars. Avoid: alarm clocks.\nWin: 'You caught 15. The party is saved.'
what_we_need_from_the_giver: 3 or more obsessions (good items), 2 harmless annoyances (bad items), and a character.
watch_outs: Dragging is hard on small phones: allow tap-left/right and an easy mode with slow drops. No fail state. Large touch targets.

when_it_makes_sense: - A competitive or fitness person: 'Rep counter'\n- Kids: 'Tap the cake'\n- A coffee lover: 'Shots pulled'
example_in_action: Tap 1: 'Warm-up.'  Tap 5: 'Feeling it?'\nTap 10: 'Confetti. Cardio is a lie.'\nTap 30: 'Please sit down. Have a biscuit.'
what_we_need_from_the_giver: One habit that can be 'trained' or counted, plus 2 or 3 related facts.
watch_outs: Fast repeated tapping can strain hands: celebrate early and stop the count from mattering. No fitness or weight shaming. Provide a mute button.

when_it_makes_sense: - Coffee and tea drinkers: cups until launch\n- Runners: kilometres to the cake\n- Bookworms: pages read
example_in_action: Cup 1: 'Awake-ish.'  Cup 5: 'Vibrating.'\nCup 8: 'Can see through time.'\nThen: 'It was decaf.' (reset)
what_we_need_from_the_giver: One obsession with a natural unit, and its funniest 'side effect'.
watch_outs: No alcohol themes for kids or anyone sober. Keep caffeine gags gentle. Let the giver pick the meter theme.

when_it_makes_sense: - Kids and grandparents playing together\n- Someone with a strong 'world': gardener, cyclist, cook\n- A calm, low-pressure game
example_in_action: Pair: trowel + rosebush. Note: 'Fourteen bushes. Every one has a name.'\nFinish: 'You matched them all. Nan's garden salutes you.'
what_we_need_from_the_giver: 6 or 8 real objects, places or people, with one line about each.
watch_outs: Use icon plus text labels for accessibility. Keep tiles large. No timer.

gender_fit: Neutral. Default arcade look can read 'gamer': re-skin it.
when_it_makes_sense: - A sporty or competitive person: the marker is a bike, ball or dart\n- Kids and teens who like escalating speed\n- A barista, chef or driver with a 'timing' habit
example_in_action: Round 1: stop the cyclist at the cafe door.\nMISS: 'Past the cafe again.'\nPERFECT: 'Caffeinated. Correct.'
what_we_need_from_the_giver: One habit tied to timing or a place, plus a marker character.
watch_outs: Timing games frustrate some players: no fail state, allow unlimited retries, and give a warm final line regardless.

when_it_makes_sense: - Kids' parties and family cards\n- A card that includes redeemable gifts (pair with Coupon Book)\n- Any adult who likes a little chance
example_in_action: Segments: 'Dinner on me', '10 minute grace period', 'One free hug', 'Snack veto'.\nResult: 'You won the last biscuit.'
what_we_need_from_the_giver: 3 gifts the giver can truly deliver, 3 real jokes, and 2 warm messages.
watch_outs: Must never look like gambling: no money, no odds language, prizes are gifts and jokes. Provide a button alternative to flicking.

when_it_makes_sense: - Crossword fans: Mum and her Sunday crossword\n- Kids: a word search of pets and favourite things\n- Quiet people who love a slow puzzle
example_in_action: 3 Across: 'Where the tomatoes live (5)' = PATCH.\nBonus when done: 'Happy birthday, Mum.'
what_we_need_from_the_giver: 8 to 10 words from their world (names, places, hobbies), with a clue for each.
watch_outs: Needs a grid generator and a validator. Answers must be A to Z: accents, hyphens and other alphabets need care. Use big tap targets for older hands.

when_it_makes_sense: - The recipient who loves being 'known'\n- Group cards: guests answer 'How well do you know Jamie?'\n- Kids: picture answers about their favourites
example_in_action: Q3: Jamie's default excuse? A) Traffic  B) 'Ten minutes out'  C) A goose was involved.\nCorrect: B. Reaction: 'Of course.'
what_we_need_from_the_giver: 6 real facts the giver can confirm, and 1 warm question. Works for the recipient or for guests.
watch_outs: Wrong answers create embarrassment: ask the giver to confirm every fact. Never quiz on sensitive topics. Picture answers for young children.

when_it_makes_sense: - Teens and adults who live online\n- Anyone with a catchphrase or tic: 'I am not late'\n- Coworker cards
example_in_action: Select all squares with snacks: bagel, bike bell, cheddar, traffic cone, croissant...\nStamp: 'Verified human. Suspiciously punctual? No.'
what_we_need_from_the_giver: One object obsession (tiles), one habit (checkbox gag), and one fact only they would know.
watch_outs: Never copy a real CAPTCHA brand or logo. Not a real security check. No data collected.

when_it_makes_sense: - Kids 8 to 14 and family cards\n- Party-game friends\n- A long car ride
example_in_action: 'Jamie pedalled to the [place] carrying [number] bags of [food], singing [silly_word] at every [noun].'
what_we_need_from_the_giver: 4 or more facts for the story spine, and the recipient's age (to keep the words age-appropriate).
watch_outs: Typed words can be rude: filter them and do not save them. Grown-ups may need to type for under-7s.

when_it_makes_sense: - Milestone birthdays: 30, 40, 50, 60, 70\n- Grandparents who love nostalgia\n- Trivia fans
example_in_action: Opener: 'Here is what was going on the year you arrived.'\nItem: [number one song from the data pack]. Line: 'You have hummed it ever since.'
what_we_need_from_the_giver: Birth year (giver confirms they want it shown) and a vetted data pack for that year.
watch_outs: Needs a vetted data pack: the model must not recall prices, songs or events. Some people keep their age private: confirm the giver wants the year shown.

gender_fit: Neutral. Choose the style from taste, not gender.
when_it_makes_sense: - Kids: a silly song with their name\n- Parents and grandparents: a gentle ballad or lullaby\n- Friends: a punk or disco roast
example_in_action: Chorus: 'Ten minutes out, it's fine, we'll wait.\nHappy birthday, Jamie, worth the wait.'
what_we_need_from_the_giver: A style preference or mood, 4 or more facts, and the recipient's catchphrase if there is one.
watch_outs: Original lyrics only: no copying real songs. Audio needs a tap to start: always show the lyrics as captions. Keep the volume sane and offer a mute.

when_it_makes_sense: - Music lovers, teens and kids\n- Drummers and DJ friends\n- A card people keep playing with
example_in_action: Pads: 'Espresso hiss' (hat), 'Bike bell' (bell), 'Ten minutes' (voice), 'Snack crunch' (snare).
what_we_need_from_the_giver: 8 real things or phrases to turn into pad names.
watch_outs: Audio needs a tap to start. Provide visual pad flashes for people who cannot hear. Lower the master volume by default.

when_it_makes_sense: - Grandparents and long-distance family\n- Kids hearing messages from far-away relatives\n- A group card where 5 friends each leave 30 seconds
example_in_action: Tape 1: 'Nan says hi' (0:28).\nTape 2: 'Brian, the actual story' (0:41).\nTape 3: 'Tim, singing badly' (0:19).
what_we_need_from_the_giver: 3 to 6 short recordings (30 to 90 seconds) from real people, plus their names.
watch_outs: Needs mic permission and consent from every speaker. Embedded audio grows the downloadable file: cap at about 90 seconds each. Provide a transcript for accessibility.

when_it_makes_sense: - Someone known for a saying: 'It's fine, I'll meet you there'\n- Kids: sound buttons like 'Boing' and 'Roar'\n- Teens: a meme-style soundboard
example_in_action: Buttons: 'It's fine' / 'Ten minutes' / 'I'll meet you there' / 'Is there any coffee?'\nSecret: 'It's fine. We'll meet you there. We always do.'
what_we_need_from_the_giver: 3 or more real catchphrases, and optionally recordings.
watch_outs: A browser voice can sound robotic: recordings are better. Show the text on screen. Never use someone's voice without their consent.

when_it_makes_sense: - Every card: the emotional peak before the finale\n- A parent to a child, read aloud\n- A long friendship: 'the real reason'
example_in_action: 'Jamie, the snacks were never the point. It's that when you turn up, the whole trip changes shape. Happy 40th. Brian and Tim.'\nP.S. We started without you.
what_we_need_from_the_giver: The reason the giver adores them (the real point of the card), 1 real story, and how the giver signs.
watch_outs: Never invent feelings: the giver approves the letter before publishing. Plain beats sappy. For young children, an adult reads it aloud.

when_it_makes_sense: - Milestone birthdays: 30, 40, 50, 60\n- A child's card from a parent: 'Nine reasons'\n- A partner's card with sincere, specific reasons
example_in_action: Counter races to 40. It stops at '4. You always ask about my day.' Then '17. The snacks.' Finally '40. Because you turn up.'
what_we_need_from_the_giver: 6 to 8 real reasons the giver loves them (small, specific ones are best), plus the age.
watch_outs: Keep the count-up under 8 seconds; for 80+ speed it up. Do not make the age itself the joke unless the giver says that is OK.

when_it_makes_sense: - Parents, partners and siblings offering real help\n- Kids giving to parents: 'One tidy room'\n- Friends: 'One airport run, any hour'
example_in_action: 'One airport run, any hour.'\n'One free bike tune-up.'\n'One 'told you so' (unused).'
what_we_need_from_the_giver: 3 or more things the giver will actually do, and 2 jokes.
watch_outs: Coupons are promises: only offer what the giver will do. No redemption backend is needed (a mailto or a screenshot works). No costly or romantic offers by default.

when_it_makes_sense: - A team or friend-group card\n- A big family milestone: 70th or 80th with many contributors\n- A class card for a teacher
example_in_action: A wall of 14 notes: 'Happy 40th!' from Tim, a doodle from Priya, a voice note from Nan.
what_we_need_from_the_giver: Names or emails of contributors, a deadline, and the recipient's basics.
watch_outs: Needs a collection flow: deadlines, moderation, a way to remove a note, consent from each contributor. Child-safety checks on doodles and photos. The wall must stay private to the link.

when_it_makes_sense: - Any age: low effort, high charm\n- When the interview gave few facts\n- A sweet bonus before the ending
example_in_action: 'You will arrive ten minutes late to your own party. The party will wait.'\nLucky numbers: 40, 3, 11, 27.
what_we_need_from_the_giver: Very little: 2 habits and the age. Great for sparse interviews.
watch_outs: Keep predictions obviously silly: nothing about health, money or love. Keep the cookie shape simple to tap.

when_it_makes_sense: - Group cards as an opener or closer\n- Families: 'Top 5 Nan-isms'\n- A teacher's card from the class
example_in_action: #5 Your playlists. #4 Your bike bell. #3 The night we missed the last train. #2 How you remember everyone's coffee. #1 You turn up.
what_we_need_from_the_giver: 5 real things (funny ones first, a story, and one sincere reason).
watch_outs: Allow 'skip to #1'. Drumroll sound optional and quiet.

when_it_makes_sense: - Tech-loving people (and anyone who likes a big red button)\n- Kids: 'Blast off the birthday'\n- Team cards: 'Deploy birthday to production'
example_in_action:
[DEPLOY BIRTHDAY]
Compiling cake... OK
Loading punctuality... skipped
Merging 40 candles... OK
Release ready.
what_we_need_from_the_giver: A theme that suits them (tech, space, kitchen) and 3 or more habits to work in as 'tasks'.
watch_outs: Keep sounds short and offer a mute. The button is harmless: no 'delete' or 'destroy' language. Reduced-motion users get the lines without shaking.

when_it_makes_sense: - Any age: the emotional beat before the final greeting\n- Kids: blow into the mic and cheer\n- A quiet, sincere card: candles out one by one
example_in_action: Nine candles are lit: '+31 more, we ran out of cake.' Tap each out: 'One down. Two...' Final: 'Happy birthday, Jamie.'
what_we_need_from_the_giver: Age, and one thing about the cake or the celebration (their favourite flavour, a running joke).
watch_outs: The mic is optional: always offer a tap fallback. Do not display the exact age if the giver flags age as private. Some people do not celebrate birthdays: let the giver skip this section.

when_it_makes_sense: - Every card ending\n- Group cards where each contributor gets a credit\n- Teens who like hidden extras
example_in_action:
Directed by Brian and Tim.
Snack Logistics: Jamie.
Punctuality Consultant: (position vacant).
No bicycles were harmed.
what_we_need_from_the_giver: Real names of the giver(s) and the friends who helped, and 2 or 3 running jokes.
watch_outs: Only credit people who agreed to be named. Credits must stop scrolling for slow readers (tap to pause).

when_it_makes_sense: - Game-loving recipients: kids, teens, adults\n- Long cards with many sections\n- When you want people to replay the card
example_in_action: 'Punctual? No.' (open the card)\n'Bark Whisperer' (tap the dog 10 times)\n'100%: Loved' (see everything)
what_we_need_from_the_giver: A few running jokes and the card's other sections (the triggers come from them).
watch_outs: Throttle pop-ups to one every 3 seconds so they do not cover the card. Provide a list view. Sound optional.
